name: BRAWNDO Hydration Depot
address: 1 Electrolyte Way, Bay 14, Dock C, Sundale Commerce Annex, Lot 7700
about: BRAWNDO Hydration Depot supplies electrolytes at residential, municipal, and watershed scale. It's got what you crave, and it has had it since the founding of the depot. Water is available elsewhere.

items.name: The Personal Drum
items.desc: Fifteen gallons, sized for one adult and their immediate obligations. It's got electrolytes.
items.imagePrompt: Ultra-premium commercial food photography for a delivery-app menu tile. Subject: a squat fifteen-gallon electric-cyan sports-drink drum, lid cracked open, luminous cyan liquid surging over the rim and sheeting down the ribbed sidewall into a spreading puddle, a thick foam collar sagging over the bung, condensation beading across the plastic. Three-quarter hero angle from slightly below so the drum looms. Setting: an industrial warehouse floor with stacked blue plastic drums and carbon-fiber panels, hazard-yellow floor striping. Lighting: hard cyan rim light with hazard-yellow kicker, wet condensation highlights, electrical arc glow, aggressive high-contrast product photography. Camera: 50mm, f/4, deep contrast, crisp speculars. Square crop, subject centered and filling the frame. Deadpan hyperreal advertising realism. No text, no logos, no packaging labels, no hands, no people.

items.imagePrompt: A careless snapshot taken on an old cheap smartphone by a restaurant employee to upload to a food delivery app. Subject: A fifty-five-gallon depot drum stood upright on a wooden pallet, brimful, its ring clamp seated and cyan electrolyte slopped over the shoulder in drying streaks down the ribbed sidewall to a puddle on the concrete. Frontal on-camera flash with no light source visible in frame, a hard blown-out hotspot on the wet lid and a hard shadow thrown behind the drum. Framed slightly crooked, the pallet cut off at the right edge, a stainless prep counter and a leaning stack of drum lids behind it.. EVERYTHING in the frame equally sharp from the food to the back wall - no shallow depth of field, no bokeh, no blurred background, no food styling. Aggressive default smartphone HDR processing: over-sharpened with visible halos along every edge, shadows lifted grey and blotchy, mushy chroma noise, heavy JPEG compression, slightly wrong white balance. The container is off-centre and clipped by one edge of the frame, the camera tilted several degrees off level, shot from too close and slightly above. This is a careless snapshot, NOT a photograph: no artistic composition, no cinematic lighting, no colour grading, no professional food photography, nothing centred or plated. Unstyled, unretouched, honest and a little unappetising - but the food is real food from a real kitchen, generous and identifiable, not a joke about bad food. Square crop.
